title: Make vs n8n
summary: Compare Make and n8n by workflow billing unit, hosting responsibility and the operational work your automation requires.

sections.heading: Estimate the same workload in each billing unit
paragraphs: Make describes credits at the module-action level. n8n Cloud describes workflow executions, where a complete run counts once regardless of its number of steps. Sketch one real automation, include retries and schedule frequency, then estimate both units from the same event volume.

sections.heading: Assign the hosting work
paragraphs: n8n documents self-hosted options as well as its Cloud service. This content record has no verified Make self-hosting fact; treat a private-network or self-hosting requirement as an open question to resolve with Make, not as proof that the capability is absent.

sections.heading: Run a failure-path trial
paragraphs: Test one integration with a rate limit, a malformed response and a credential rotation. Record retry behavior, run history, alerting and the time required to recover the workflow before selecting a platform.

pros.text: Make distinguishes fixed from dynamic credit consumption, so a representative scenario can be estimated against documented usage rules.
n8n Cloud uses workflow executions as its billing unit; one workflow run is counted regardless of its number of steps.

cons.text: Make credit use can vary for AI and advanced modules with tokens, file size, pages or processing time.
n8n self-hosting does not establish lower operating cost; the operator must also configure transport and at-rest encryption.

faqs.question: Can I compare one Make credit directly with one n8n execution?
faqs.answer: No. Make credits can depend on the module and workload, while n8n Cloud counts a workflow execution once per complete run. Map the same trigger, steps and retries into both units.

faqs.question: Does n8n self-hosting establish a lower total cost?
faqs.answer: No. The documentation establishes a self-hosted deployment option, not a cost conclusion; confirm license fit and operating requirements for the intended deployment.

faqs.question: Does self-hosting mean no data is processed by n8n?
faqs.answer: No. n8n's policy says it processes certain usage data from self-hosted deployments unless users opt out. Check the instance setting and the terms of connected services separately.

verdict: Choose from the measured workload and hosting requirement. Make's credit unit and n8n's execution unit are not directly comparable without mapping the same automation into each billing model.
bestFor: Automation builders comparing task-based visual scenarios with API-oriented workflows
notFor: Teams choosing on a quoted total cost before confirming billing cadence, plan limits and hosting requirements
migration: Rebuild one non-critical automation first. Export what the vendor supports, re-enter credentials through approved secret handling, and verify schedules, retries and outputs before switching traffic.
gaps: For 10,000 monthly credits, Make lists USD 12/month with monthly payment or USD 9/month equivalent on annual billing; confirm regional checkout taxes and the workload-specific credit requirement before setting a budget.
Confirm license compatibility and the self-hosted operating cost for the intended n8n use.
Verify n8n self-hosted telemetry opt-out and connected-service data terms; no instance configuration was inspected.
